Unauthorized Access to Document Storage [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on S3 Document Bucket, S3 Archive Bucket, IAM Roles, CloudFront Distribution: Attackers might attempt to access S3 buckets directly using stolen credentials, misconfigured IAM policies, or by exploiting public access settings. An attacker obtains temporary AWS credentials through a compromised application instance and uses them to directly access the S3 buckets containing sensitive documents.

SQL Injection in Document Metadata Processing [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-89] on RDS PostgreSQL Database, ECS Fargate Tasks, Lambda Functions: Malicious actors could attempt to inject SQL commands through metadata fields when uploading documents, which if not properly sanitized could be executed against the RDS database. An attacker uploads a document with specially crafted metadata containing SQL injection payloads that could extract sensitive data or modify database contents.

Sensitive Data Exposure in Logs [Information Disclosure, CWE-532] on CloudWatch Logs, Lambda Functions, ECS Tasks, Application Code: Application code or Lambda functions might log document contents or metadata for debugging purposes, inadvertently exposing sensitive information in CloudWatch Logs. An attacker with access to CloudWatch Logs could extract sensitive information from log entries containing document contents or user PII.

Key Management and Rotation Weaknesses [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-320] on KMS Keys, RDS Database, S3 Buckets, Secrets Manager: Static encryption keys or insufficient rotation policies could allow attackers to decrypt data if they obtain the keys through compromise or extraction. An attacker who obtains a static encryption key could potentially decrypt historical data even after the key is rotated if proper re-encryption isn't performed.

Session Management Vulnerabilities [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, CWE-384] on DynamoDB Sessions Table, Application Code, Redis Cache: Attackers might attempt to steal or forge session tokens, or exploit weaknesses in token refresh mechanisms to maintain unauthorized access. An attacker captures a session token through XSS or network interception and uses it to impersonate the user even after the original session should have expired.

Document Processing Race Conditions [Tampering, Denial of Service, CWE-362] on SQS Queue, Lambda Functions, ECS Tasks, S3 Buckets: Concurrent processing of the same document by multiple processors could lead to race conditions, resulting in data corruption or inconsistent state. Multiple document processors attempt to modify the same document simultaneously, leading to corrupt output or lost updates.

Insecure Direct Object References [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-639] on Application Code, CloudFront Distribution, S3 Buckets: Attackers might manipulate document identifiers in URLs or API calls to access documents they shouldn't have permission to view. An attacker modifies document IDs in requests to access other users' documents by guessing or incrementing ID values.
